key_insight: A causal-adversarial probe can distinguish clinical covariates that add useful disease signal from those that mainly act as non-generalising shortcuts in prostate MRI grade prediction.
clinical_relevance: This approach may help build more robust prostate MRI grading models by identifying which patient factors should be suppressed versus retained during model development.
method: Treat MRI appearance and ISUP grade as observations of latent tumour pathology rather than a direct cause-effect chain.
Adversarially suppress the decodability of one clinical covariate at a time while keeping MRI-based grade prediction strong.
Compare performance changes to label covariates as nuisance, proxy, or task-relevant signal.
evidence_signal: The framework was evaluated on 2,903 prostate MRI exams with external validation on 576 patients; suppressing age, BMI, and alcohol use improved AUC, while suppressing PSA and prostate volume reduced AUC.
watch_item: Adversarial suppression can indicate representation dependence, but it does not by itself prove causality or guarantee improved real-world generalisation across all sites and scanners.
paper_title: Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading
